ticket.model_delta_expectation: ZERO. Document the no-op model result with evidence.
ticket.model_delta_result: ZERO, as expected and verified. AC-04 adds no state variable, no action and no invariant: the delta is a scanner over the source tree and the ledger, and `architecture_scan` already exists from AC-01. Ticket current and desired are byte-identical and both match specs/current for TlaSpecDevCli.tla, MC.cfg and spec_manifest.yaml (md5s recorded in model-delta.txt); variables 10, actions 16, bound 2,799,360, modularity 0.0 in all three trees and in the previous recorded entry (AC-03). TLC green at 32,122,220 generated / 1,292,951 distinct / depth 26 in 59s, identical to AC-01's and AC-03's runs.
ticket.objective: Make a refactor measurable instead of hoped-for. `--baseline` on the architecture scan compares two runs and reports the divergence delta with the specific edges gained and lost; the delta joins the complexity ledger as a RECORDED, NON-GATING member alongside the CD-09 fuzzing-era members, so a ticket that increased structural divergence is visible in its close evidence and one that lowered it can prove it. Extend the validated-refactor basis (CD-02/CD-09) with the code-structure half: TLC green before and after, behavior corpus unchanged, descriptor comparison recorded, AND the divergence delta recorded. State plainly what makes a refactor safe here -- the generated corpus plus effect providers with content assertions (ex1-run4: 45 points killed on the exact MF-038 bug class) -- and what does not (the kill rate, which MF-038 falsified as a bug-catching claim).
ticket.result: The delta ships and its refusals hold on this repository. `--baseline` on `analyze architecture` reports the divergence delta with the specific dependencies gained and lost (unit: distinct (from, to, kind, symbol); the line number is excluded so a reformatting does not read as churn), and the ledger records it as `architecture_delta` -- derived from the report file, not typed by the author, and gating nothing. Three measured results. (1) The loop on a real change: baseline scan of e610b98, this ticket's implementation, rescan -- attribution `code_only` with identical map and model digests, divergences 0 -> 0, convergences 93 -> 95 with both gained dependencies enumerated at file:line (complexity_ledger.py -> spec_paths.py, import and call; a pair the model ports). (2) The gaming move, refused: re-placing scripts/budgets.py from `surface` to `kill` in the map alone moves this repository's divergence count 0 -> 6 with no source change, and the delta across that pair reports `unattributable` with the re-placement named and every lost edge classified `endpoint_reassigned`, instead of a six-edge improvement. (3) MF-020 applied to structure: a drop whose lost edges are not enumerated, or whose endpoints merely stopped being mapped, is `unverified`, never `improved`; a drop explained only by deleted files is `improved` with a RED FLAG. What is NOT shown: no real divergence was removed on a real tree, because this repository has none under the declared partition -- the `improved` path is exercised only on fixtures, and the headline number here cannot move for most changes to this repo.
